explanation: He picked it because it appeared on keyboards but almost never in names. Many languages give it playful names: Italians call it chiocciola, snail, and Dutch speakers apenstaartje, little monkey's tail.

claims.text: In 1971 Ray Tomlinson chose the @ sign to separate the user's name from the host computer's name in email addresses.
Tomlinson did not choose the hash sign, the ampersand or the dot for this.
Tomlinson chose @ because it was on keyboards but was not used in people's names.
In Italian the @ sign is called chiocciola, which means snail.
In Dutch the @ sign is called apenstaartje, which means little monkey's tail.
